summary.one_liner: A Docker container image that automatically downloads, installs, and runs Windows (and many legacy versions) inside a KVM-accelerated virtual machine, viewed through a web browser or RDP.
summary.what_it_does: Runs a Windows virtual machine inside a Docker container, downloading the selected Windows ISO and installing it hands-free. Users pick a version with the VERSION environment variable, covering Windows 11, 10, 8.1, 7, Vista, XP, 2000, ME, 98, 95, Windows Server 2003 to 2025, Tiny11/Tiny10 and ReactOS. The installed system is reachable through a web viewer on port 8006 and via RDP on port 3389. Configuration covers CPU cores, RAM, disk size, multiple disks, disk and USB passthrough, host folder sharing, audio streaming, and Active Directory domain join. Networking options include NAT, user-mode, macvlan and macvtap, with an optional DHCP mode so Windows gets its own router-assigned IP. Memory ballooning is available for dynamic RAM allocation.
use_cases: Run Windows in a container on a Linux server
Test software on old Windows versions like XP or 98
Spin up a disposable Windows VM with Docker Compose
Run Windows Server for lab or Active Directory testing
Provide a Windows backend for WinBoat, WinApps or WinPodX
Access a Windows desktop from a browser or RDP client
how_to_run: Install Docker or Podman on a Linux host with KVM support
Create a compose file with image dockurr/windows, VERSION set (e.g. "11"), /dev/kvm and /dev/net/tun devices, NET_ADMIN capability, and ports 8006 and 3389
Mount a volume to /storage for the VM data

Or run: docker run -it --rm --name windows -e "VERSION=11" -p 8006:8006 --device=/dev/kvm --device=/dev/net/tun --cap-add NET_ADMIN -v "${PWD:-.}/windows:/storage" --stop-timeout 120 docker.io/dockurr/windows
Open http://localhost:8006 in a browser and wait for the automatic installation to finish
Optionally connect with an RDP client using username Docker and password admin
notable: Fully automatic, hands-free Windows installation from a VERSION setting, with no manual ISO handling
Supports a wide range of releases from Windows 95 and XP through Windows 11 and Server 2025
Optional macvlan and DHCP mode gives the Windows VM its own IP address on the home network
Serves as the backend for desktop integration projects WinBoat, WinPodX and WinApps
Memory ballooning and USB passthrough options
caveats: Requires KVM access (/dev/kvm); Docker Desktop on Linux, macOS, and Windows 10 is not supported because containers lack KVM access
Needs at least 2 GB RAM and 32 GB free disk; default disk is 64 GB and default RAM allocation is 4 GB
The README says the web viewer is mainly for installation and RDP is recommended for daily use; audio is off unless enabled
Windows licensing is the user's responsibility; the project does not distribute Windows
keywords: share files with host windows vm
